title: Hierarchical injectors
description: Learn how Angular's hierarchical injector system resolves dependencies through component and environment hierarchies.

blocks.text: Injectors in Angular have rules that govern how they locate and instantiate dependencies. Angular has a hierarchical injection system, which means that injectors can be nested in a tree structure mirroring your component hierarchy.
There are two main injector hierarchies in Angular:

items: EnvironmentInjector hierarchy: Configured at the application root level (via ApplicationConfig.providers or route-level providers).
NodeInjector hierarchy: Created invisibly at each DOM element where a component or directive is declared (via @Component.providers).

blocks.text: When a component requests a dependency, Angular first searches the local NodeInjector. If not found, it traverses upward through parent component NodeInjectors until it reaches the root, then searches the EnvironmentInjector hierarchy up to the platform injector.
